output.name: Hanor

anatomy.part: right end of the hanging bone bar
left end of the bar, where the cord is tied on
knot on the cord, halfway down
crown of the stone, where the cord enters the bob
point of the stone, the tip

output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky went up so fast that his sister Sil had to run after it along the tide. Before he could let go, he had tied a stone to the last of the line, so he would know how far the sky had fallen from the islands. Hesk saw what he had done and kept count of it on her reel. Hanor is that stone. It still swings in the Leeward dark on a line hung from a bar of bone. Each night it hangs a little straighter. The old ones say that when it hangs plumb, the sky will stand up again and come home. Tavo the Gale tries to knock it sideways for sport, and sometimes he does. Then the sailors say the sea has moved under them, and they fall to their knees. Mind your own line, the grandmothers say. Tie a stone to what you fear losing, so you know where it went.
output.verse:
Hanor swings below,
the stone keeps count of each fall,
plumb, the sky will stand.

problems: The blind guess (spoon or ladle) is only loosely right. The structure fits, a long cord with a weight at the bottom, but the bob is a small quadrilateral, not a bowl, so nothing makes it read as a plumb-line.
The hanging bar is a thin, nearly flat horizontal stroke at the top (64962 near (323,108), 64166 near (373,108)). It does not read as a solid bar.

The stone is too small relative to the cord: about 40 px tall against a cord about 300 px long. The tip (65535 near (280,471)) and shoulders (64408 near (341,431), 65936 near (259,463)) do not form a clear weighted bob with a point facing down.

Labels collide. The two top labels ('left end of the bar' and 'right end of the hanging bone') print on top of each other, and the 'left shoulder' and 'point of the stone' labels overlap. Several labels are clipped ('where th', 'halfway do').
Orientation is correct: bar at top, bob hanging at the bottom.

The blue outlines around the bar and stone suggest a separate silhouette, but the bob outline sits so close to the gold lines that it is hard to tell whether a real silhouette is drawn or the gold lines are traced. The stars do sit on the intended parts: knot 64803 near (325,292) is halfway down the cord, and crown 65109 near (305,405) is where the cord meets the bob.
judge.advice: Redraw the bob as a solid, clearly weighted stone. Place the crown (65109) near (305,405). Build a cone or drop below it: right shoulder 64408 out to about (345,430), left shoulder 65936 out to about (255,462), and the tip 65535 at the bottom near (280,478), so the point faces straight down under the crown. Make the bob roughly 60 to 80 px tall. Draw the bar as a solid rectangle from 64962 near (323,108) to 64166 near (373,108), with some thickness. Stagger the top labels so they do not overlap, and shorten or wrap the clipped labels.

guess: A long-handled spoon or ladle, with a bowl at the bottom and a flat capsule-shaped end at the top
